BlogPage.istExcerpt: One enormous terminal, a young metro link, and taxi queues — how to move through IST with confidence.

BlogPage.pointsTitle: Points transfers 101: turning card points into flights
BlogPage.pointsExcerpt: What the transfer options on each Tern flight actually mean, and three rules before you move points.
BlogPage.pointsIntro: Next to each flight, Tern shows what that fare could cost in transferred card points. Here is how to read those numbers — and when not to trust any points math blindly.
BlogPage.pointsHow: The options come from public transfer ratios between major card programs and airline partners. They are estimates for comparing value; the actual transfer and award booking always happen inside your card and airline accounts.
BlogPage.pointsTip1: Transfer only after you can see award space. Transfers are one-way; points parked in an airline program lose flexibility.
BlogPage.pointsTip2: Compare against the cash fare every time. If the cents-per-point value is poor, paying cash and keeping points is winning.
BlogPage.pointsTip3: Transfer bonuses appear and vanish monthly. The program pages, not third-party posts, are the source of truth.
BlogPage.rankTitle: How Tern ranks flights: the five smart picks explained
BlogPage.rankExcerpt: Cheapest, Fastest, Earliest arrival, AI pick, Lowest delay risk — what each label does and doesn't promise.
BlogPage.rankIntro: Every search on Tern surfaces five picks. None of them is 'the best flight' — each optimizes exactly one thing, and says so.
BlogPage.rankCheapestBody: The lowest total fare in the results, nothing else considered. Long layovers and red-eyes included.
BlogPage.rankFastestBody: Shortest door-to-door travel time. Often costs more; the gap to Cheapest tells you what your hours are priced at.
BlogPage.rankEarliestBody: Lands first, regardless of departure time or price — useful when a meeting, not a budget, is the constraint.
BlogPage.rankAIBody: A weighted balance of price, duration, and arrival. It is a compromise by design — check what it traded away.
BlogPage.rankDelayBody: A relative estimate from the itinerary's shape — stops, red-eye departure times, and tight connections. A signal for choosing between similar flights, not live delay data, and never a guarantee — weather wins every time.

AboutPage.title: Why "Tern"
AboutPage.intro: Tern is a flight-comparison tool that puts the trade-offs side by side instead of hiding them.
AboutPage.whatBody: One search returns the cheapest fare, the fastest trip, the earliest arrival, an AI-balanced pick, and the lowest delay-risk option — plus what each fare could cost in transferred card points. You see what every choice trades away, then book through the airline or our booking partners.
AboutPage.diff1: No invented urgency. No fake countdowns, no "3 seats left" we can't verify.
AboutPage.diff2: No invented deals. Promotions link to the airline's own pages; if we can't verify a claim, we don't show it.
AboutPage.diff3: Honest risk signals. The delay-risk score is a relative estimate from the itinerary's shape — stops, timing, and connections — labeled as an estimate, never dressed up as live delay data.
AboutPage.nameBody1: The Arctic Tern flies from pole to pole every year — the longest migration of any animal we know of. It spends its life chasing summer along the most efficient route it can find.
AboutPage.nameBody2: That is the entire product idea: find the best route, honestly, and go. The boarding pass in our hero carries a tern for the same reason.

SupportPage.title: Help & FAQ
SupportPage.intro: Short answers to the questions that actually come up.
SupportPage.faq1q: How does the flight search work?
SupportPage.faq1a: Search results are live offers from our flight-data partner, fetched at the moment you search. Prices are per person and refresh with every new search — a fare seen an hour ago may be gone.
SupportPage.faq2a: The points options shown next to each flight are estimates based on public transfer ratios between card programs and airlines. Tern doesn't move your points — the transfer and the award booking happen in your card and airline accounts.
SupportPage.faq3q: How do refunds and changes work?
SupportPage.faq3a: Bookings complete on the airline's site or our checkout partner's page, and that fare's own rules govern refunds and changes. Check the fare conditions before paying — Tern compares flights but never holds your ticket.
SupportPage.faq4q: What does the delay-risk number mean?
SupportPage.faq4a: It's a relative estimate built from the itinerary's shape — the number of stops, red-eye departure times, and tight connections. Use it to compare similar flights, not as a prediction for your specific day. It isn't live or historical delay data.
SupportPage.faq5q: Why is the final price sometimes different?
SupportPage.faq5a: Airlines reprice fares continuously, and the booking page always shows the authoritative amount. Currency conversions on Tern are for display and may differ slightly from your card's rate.
SupportPage.faq6a: Set a target price on a route and Tern checks new search results against it. Alerts live in your browser on this device — they don't follow you across devices yet.
SupportPage.contactBody: Email us — a human reads these.

TermsPage.title: Terms of Use
TermsPage.intro: The plain-language terms for using Tern — no dark patterns, no fine print that contradicts what the product actually does.
TermsPage.s1p: Tern (flytern.site) is an independent flight-search and comparison tool, built and run by a solo developer. It is not a travel agency or an airline, and it does not sell or issue tickets itself.
TermsPage.s2p: Tern searches live fares through the Duffel API and highlights the cheapest, fastest, earliest, lowest-delay-risk, and best-value-with-points options. Prices and availability come from third parties and change constantly, so every result is indicative — always confirm the final price and conditions on the provider's own site before you pay.
TermsPage.s3p: Tern does not take payment or issue tickets. When you continue to book, you are handed off to a third party who becomes your counterparty: Duffel Links (Duffel is the merchant of record and ticketing runs under its accreditation; this checkout currently runs in test mode, so no real tickets are issued), our partner booking site at book.flytern.site (Aviasales inventory via Travelpayouts), or an airline's own site. Your booking contract is with that provider, and their terms and refund or change rules apply.
TermsPage.s4h: Affiliate links and how we make money
TermsPage.s4p: Some outbound links are affiliate links: if you book after following one, Tern may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never changes how results are ranked — search results are ordered only by the sort you choose (price, duration, or fewest stops), and Tern shows no fabricated discounts, coupons, or 'sponsored' badges.
TermsPage.s5p: Please use Tern for personal, non-automated flight research. Don't scrape, overload, resell, or reverse-engineer the service, and don't use it to break any law or a provider's terms. Because this is an actively developed personal project, features may change or be removed.
TermsPage.s6p: Tern is provided 'as is', with no guarantee that fares, schedules, or other data are accurate, complete, or available at any given moment. To the extent the law allows, Tern and its developer are not liable for losses arising from third-party providers, data errors, or service interruptions. Nothing here limits rights you have that cannot be waived.
TermsPage.s7p: These terms may be updated as the product evolves; the effective date above shows the latest version.

PrivacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPage.intro: What Tern collects, what it doesn't, and who else is involved — in the same plain language as the rest of the site.
PrivacyPage.contactLead: Questions, or want your data removed? Email
PrivacyPage.s1p: Tern (flytern.site) is run by a solo developer, who is responsible for the data described here.
PrivacyPage.s2p:
Account: if you sign in, authentication is handled by Firebase Authentication (Google), which stores your email address and, for Google sign-in, basic profile details.
Searches: the origin, destination, dates, and passenger counts you enter are sent to Tern's search API and on to Duffel to fetch fares; airport, weather, currency, and location lookups go to the providers that power those features.
Preferences: your chosen language is kept in a cookie, and any price alerts you create are stored only in your own browser — they never reach Tern's servers.
PrivacyPage.s3p: Tern runs no third-party analytics, advertising, or cross-site tracking, sets no advertising cookies, and does not sell or rent your data. You won't get marketing email — the only mail is a reply if you write in first.
PrivacyPage.s4p: A few processors handle specific jobs: Firebase/Google (sign-in), Duffel (fares and hosted checkout), Travelpayouts/Aviasales (the partner booking site), and the weather, currency, and geocoding providers behind those features. Support email to flytern.site is delivered through Namecheap's email forwarding. Any payment is taken by the booking provider at checkout — Tern never sees or stores card details.
PrivacyPage.s5p: Tern uses only what it needs: a cookie to remember your language, your sign-in session if you log in, and your browser's local storage to hold price alerts on your device. There are no advertising or analytics cookies to consent to.
PrivacyPage.s6p: You can sign out at any time, clear saved price alerts by clearing them in your browser, and ask for your account and email to be deleted by writing to support. Because searches are passed straight to providers to return results, they aren't kept as a personal profile on Tern's side.
PrivacyPage.s7p: Personal data is kept only as long as it's needed for the purpose it was given — account data until you ask us to delete it. This policy may change as the product does; the effective date above marks the current version.
